A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PITA and share the same principal experiments. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, proofs, and experimental appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original sampling experiments on LJ-13, Alanine Dipeptide, and Alanine Tripeptide, together with ablations and molecular-dynamics analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and reports additional baseline comparisons, timing measurements, and effective-sample-size diagnostics.

M1.justification: PITA's inference equations, training losses, network architectures, and progressive annealing procedure remain unchanged. Appendix J adds pseudocode describing existing inference; it does not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Cartesian-coordinate sampling on LJ-13, Alanine Dipeptide, and Alanine Tripeptide. Added comparisons and diagnostics use the existing systems and tasks.

E2.justification: The ALDP comparison adds MD-NF, FKC, and Score Scaling in Table 2, plus PT and SMC in new Table 4. Score scaling already appeared in the earlier CFG ablation, which remains, but now participates in the main comparison. Table 3 additionally evaluates relaxed TA-BG; the LJ-13 comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 separates interatomic Distance-W2 from Geometric-W2. Table 3 changes MD-Diff's AL3 energy budget from 5 × 10^7 to 8 × 10^7 and adds TA-BG relaxation at the larger budget. New experiments specify SMC/PT schedules and 30k-sample timing and ESS evaluations. The reported OpenMM temperature changes from 310 K to 300 K, without establishing whether simulations were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix F examines ESS during PITA inference without resampling, across temperature transitions and integration time. Table 3 adds a TA-BG relaxation comparison. Existing temperature-jump, schedule, loss, resampling, and MD-mixing analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain standard deviations over three seeds, with no reported increase in runs or new significance-testing procedure. ESS was already defined and reported in Appendix D.2; its new applications extend diagnostics rather than introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 relocates the iDEM/Adjoint values 1.61/1.67 from Distance-W2 to Geometric-W2, reports iDEM Distance-W2 as 0.127, and leaves Adjoint Distance-W2 unavailable. Table 3 replaces MD-Diff results under the larger budget and adds relaxed TA-BG, whose Energy-W2 is 4.863 versus 178.558 without relaxation. Other additions include baseline scores, ESS results, and inference times of 4.7/139.2/59.5 minutes for PITA/SMC/PT per 30k samples. These are corrected, additional, or changed-setting results.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–3, their proofs, endpoint corrections, and network-preconditioning mathematics are retained. The added score-scaling equations explain an operation already described in v1's CFG ablation rather than introduce a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The central claims remain progressive diffusion-based Boltzmann sampling, Cartesian peptide sampling, and reduced energy-evaluation requirements. Correcting 'progressively higher' to 'progressively lower' temperatures in the abstract aligns its wording with the procedure already described in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of amortization break-even points and inference-time ESS, including motivation for resampling and future drift modifications. It also extends the stated benefit of AL3 relaxation to TA-BG. Existing limitations concerning energy-model training, resource costs, and imperfect mode weights remain.

D1.justification: Appendices E, I, and J add SMC/PT settings, MD-NF parameterization details, explicit score-scaling equations, a 564.3-minute ALDP training time, and inference pseudocode. Existing PITA hyperparameters and the code link remain. The new listing contains inconsistencies, including div(xt) instead of the score divergence in Equation 12 and an undefined dU_dt variable.

R1.justification: v2 adds Noble et al. on sampling with known modes and Klein–Noé and Tan et al. on transferable sampling. The Boltzmann-generator discussion largely moves from the appendix into Section 4. Numerous other reference changes are publication-metadata updates, with the main positioning retained.

P1.justification: There are localized language corrections, updated author/contact and conference information, a moved Boltzmann-generator paragraph, and new appendix sections. Most existing prose and the overall argument remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially expanded: Figure 1 is redrawn, Tables 1–3 gain metric columns or comparison rows, and Figures 3 and 5 incorporate revised AL3 comparisons. New Tables 4–6 and Figure 10 present classical baselines, timings, and ESS diagnostics. Other appendix plots are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: Separating the conflated LJ-13 metrics and adding equal-budget AL3 baseline comparisons address important weaknesses in v1's empirical support. Classical SMC/PT comparisons and amortization timings substantially strengthen evaluation of the efficiency claim. The gains outweigh localized problems: broad superiority wording remains insufficiently qualified, Appendix F's stabilization claim conflicts with Figure 10's rising curve, and the new pseudocode contains errors.
